exhibits.claim: S&P 500 futures large-speculator net positioning (CFTC COT), lagged to its public release date, conditions forward returns of the equity panel: positioning extremes precede weaker or more volatile forward returns than neutral positioning
exhibits.reason: Not significant, and the return half of the claim points the WRONG WAY. L1_net_length_extreme NW t=-1.24; L2_1y_zscore NW t=-0.76; L3_wow_change NW t=-0.20 — all against a deflated bar of 2.87 (base 2.5, family n=3 from declared_looks=3). Bootstrap P(Sharpe<=0) is 0.58-0.89 against a 0.0167 bar and every margin-of-safety t is negative. Direction: the ticket predicted extremes precede WEAKER panel returns; in 3/3 looks extreme-positioning weeks earned MORE than neutral weeks (e.g. L1 26.6%/yr vs 13.1%/yr annualised), which is why the tested long-neutral/short-extreme series has a negative mean. The reverse is not claimed as an edge either: |t| never exceeds 1.24, so this is a null, not a sign flip to trade. The only part of the claim with support is the volatility half — extreme weeks run 12-21% higher panel volatility (Levene p<=0.0016, see metrics.vol_conditioning) — and a volatility regime is not a return edge and is not promotable here. Result is robust to both construction choices (naive as_of+3d alignment and fixed-0.6 weighting): no variant reaches |t|=1.3.
exhibits.about: Asks whether how crowded the futures crowd is tells you anything about what equities do next.

exhibits.claim: Kronos-small (24.7M-param K-line foundation model, zero-shot) beats expanding-window log-Parkinson HAR on 5-day realized volatility (prereg docs/kronos_vol_prereg.md, locked 2026-07-21 before any run)
exhibits.reason: Pre-registered head-to-head: HAR beats zero-shot Kronos on all 21 tickers (19/21 individually significant), pooled QLIKE 0.148 vs 0.591 (~4x), DM NW-t=-12.37. Verdict existed only in docs since 2026-07-21; filed to the store 2026-07-28 so rule 2 can prevent a retest.
exhibits.about: Asks a 25-million-parameter pretrained model to out-forecast a 20-parameter regression on volatility.

exhibits.claim: Volatility-normalised tick size conditions short-horizon trend/reversal in US large caps (Kurth-Eisler-Rej-Bouchaud 2026 transfer): high tick-to-dollar-vol names behave like the papers large-tick tier (continuation survives), low ratio like small-tick (dead or reverting)
exhibits.reason: none of the 4 declared looks clears the deflated bar (best NW t=0.10 vs t_bar=2.96, family n=4); the conditioning contrast (continuation high-minus-low, ann=6.14%, NW t=3.21) clears the deflated t bar but fails: margin-of-safety rerun (gross halved, costs doubled) t=1.64 < 2.5 — edge has no buffer; IS/OOS degradation 80% > 30% (IS 0.89 -> OOS 0.18) — overfitting signature
exhibits.about: Tests whether stocks with chunky price grids relative to their volatility trend differently from fine-grid names.

exhibits.claim: Asset-growth anomaly vs the AI capex boom: the classic high-capex-underperforms effect (Cooper-Gulen-Schill) weakens or inverts for AI-buildout leaders post-2023
exhibits.reason: neither declared look clears the joint family gate (n=2, bar t>=2.74): full-sample anomaly D1-D10 NW t=-0.71 (stressed -0.6), post-2023 inversion D10-D1 NW t=0.91 (stressed 0.33)
exhibits.about: One of the oldest anomalies says companies that grow assets fastest underperform - empire-building destroys value. The AI buildout is history's biggest capex boom since WWII (Bridgewater). Is the old rule holding, or is this the cycle that breaks it?

exhibits.claim: Peer-momentum spillover: sector/rolling-correlation-graph peer signals add return information beyond own momentum AND Moskowitz-Grinblatt industry momentum (point-in-time edges, turnover-costed)
exhibits.reason: Neither graph's peer-momentum signal carries information beyond own momentum and Moskowitz-Grinblatt industry momentum once those are residualized out cross-sectionally. Sector leave-one-out peer signal: NW t=0.27 vs deflated bar 2.74 (family n=2), bootstrap P(Sharpe<=0)=0.39, stressed t=-0.87, stage-6 residual alpha t=0.55. Corr top-10 peer signal: NW t=-1.63 (wrong sign), stage-6 alpha t=-1.40. Both fail stage 4 and stage 6 outright; not marginal.
exhibits.about: Tests whether the recent gains of a stock's connected peers predict its own next move, beyond its own trend.

exhibits.claim: Time-varying price of risk (Adrian-Crump-Moench JFE 2015 lineage): lagged price-of-risk states (VIX level, ACM term premium, term spread) forecast the FF factor premia time-series — factor timing via priced states, not constant lambdas
exhibits.reason: Newey-West t=-0.14 < 2.50 (base 2.5, family n=1); bootstrap P(Sharpe<=0)=0.5682 > 0.05 (base 0.05, family n=1); margin-of-safety rerun (gross halved, costs doubled) t=-0.07 < 2.5 — edge has no buffer; IS/OOS degradation 771% > 30% (IS 0.02 -> OOS -0.13) — overfitting signature
exhibits.about: Tests whether the market's price of fear and the bond term premium predict WHEN the classic factor strategies pay, instead of assuming they always pay the same.

exhibits.claim: Global price of risk (Adrian-Stackman-Vogt IMF ER 2019): the US-VIX-based price of risk forecasts international equity returns (EFA/EEM) with heterogeneous loadings — US fear is a global state variable
exhibits.reason: No leg clears the gates (family_n=3, deflated bar t>=2.87). EFA leg is dead (NW t=0.11). EEM leg: NW t=2.19 < 2.87, stressed t=1.09, IS/OOS degradation 37%. The heterogeneity leg (EEM-EFA, the paper's core claim) clears the deflated NW bar (t=4.19) but fails the margin-of-safety rerun (stressed t=2.10 < 2.5) and shows a 62% IS/OOS Sharpe degradation (0.95 -> 0.36) — the EM loading on US fear was real in-sample (GFC era) and has decayed. Promising but unproven is a rejection.
exhibits.about: Tests whether American fear prices the whole world's stock markets, and whether emerging markets load on it harder than developed ones.

exhibits.claim: External-financing anomaly, AI-capex edition: heavy net debt issuers among AI-buildout names underperform (BIS 2026: top-5 AI commitments now exceed free cash flow; the classic Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan effect meets the biggest debt-funded capex boom since the telecoms)
exhibits.reason: Right sign, no significance. Trailing-12m BRS net external financing (PIT from EDGAR companyfacts cash-flow XBRL, 435 tickers, 27,772 PIT events, coverage from 2010-05), quintile L/S long retirers / short heavy issuers: NW t=1.63 < deflated bar 2.74 (family capex_financing, n=2); bootstrap P(Sharpe<=0)=0.0558 > 0.025; margin-of-safety stress t=0.54 < 2.5; FF5+Mom residual alpha 0.63%/yr, t=0.77 < 2.0. AI-capex subsample shows the anomaly direction more strongly (Sharpe 0.46, ann +5.07%, t=1.78) but also fails; 'promising but unproven' is a rejection reason, not a pass.
exhibits.about: The BIS's 2026 warning in one sentence: hyperscalers flipped from cash machines to net borrowers to fund AI. The oldest financing anomaly says heavy issuers underperform. Is the oldest rule holding through the loudest capex boom - or is this the exception the borrowers are betting on?

exhibits.claim: El Nino regimes (NOAA ONI index) predict relative returns of commodity-sensitive equity sectors: energy and staples names outperform the panel during El Nino phases as food and fuel inflation passes through
exhibits.reason: Newey-West t=0.24 < 2.50 (base 2.5, family n=1); bootstrap P(Sharpe<=0)=0.7298 > 0.05 (base 0.05, family n=1); margin-of-safety rerun (gross halved, costs doubled) t=0.12 < 2.5 — edge has no buffer; IS/OOS degradation 117% > 30% (IS 0.43 -> OOS -0.07) — overfitting signature
exhibits.about: A weather cycle with a 75-year public index and a mechanical pass-through story (crops, cooling demand, hydro shortfalls). Kin to the retired sunshine study but a different animal: seasonal-scale supply shocks, not daily mood. CIBC's own rule of thumb - normal El Nino adds ~5% to commodity inflation - is the claim I make testable in equities.

exhibits.claim: Housing affordability ceiling: when the US home-price-to-income ratio is stretched (top tercile), US homebuilder stocks (DHI/LEN/PHM/NVR) subsequently underperform the panel over the next 1-2 quarters as affordability caps demand
exhibits.reason: Newey-West t=0.67 < 2.50 (base 2.5, family n=1); bootstrap P(Sharpe<=0)=0.1873 > 0.05 (base 0.05, family n=1); margin-of-safety rerun (gross halved, costs doubled) t=0.33 < 2.5 — edge has no buffer; IS/OOS degradation 171% > 30% (IS 1.91 -> OOS -1.36) — overfitting signature
exhibits.about: A global affordability map (UN Habitat via Visual Capitalist) shows the US at 4.5x income - 7th most affordable of 181 - while China sits at 34.6x. The testable US question: does a stretched domestic affordability ratio predict homebuilder underperformance? Intuitive, probably weak - a tested rejection is the likely honest outcome, and that is museum content.

exhibits.claim: Dividend-cut forced-selling overshoot (Manual of Ideas Table 8.1, 'dividend cancellation'): stocks cutting/suspending dividends overshoot to the downside on yield-seeker forced selling, then partially reverse over the next 1-3 months
exhibits.reason: reversal (tradeable) leg fails the gates: margin-of-safety rerun (gross halved, costs doubled) t=1.85 < 2.5 — edge has no buffer
exhibits.about: Table 8.1 row 3: income funds forced to sell on a dividend cut may push price below fair value, creating a reversal. Testable event study; needs a dividend-action date harvest.

exhibits.claim: Prediction markets (Kalshi) are calibrated, and one-sided books resolve against the crowd (pre-registered: docs/prediction_market_prereg.md, family n=3)
exhibits.reason: 250,858 resolved Kalshi markets across 59,748 distinct events, price = VWAP over the final 24h. C1 CALIBRATION FALSIFIED: the reliability curve departs sharply from the diagonal (reliability component 0.019 of a 0.093 Brier). C2 FAVOURITE-LONGSHOT CONFIRMED and large: contracts priced 0.30-0.40 resolve YES 17% of the time (+14 to +18 points overpriced) while contracts priced 0.60-0.70 resolve 88% (-21 to -23 points underpriced). ROBUST: holds at +0.140/-0.214 on ONE market per event (59,748 independent events, killing multi-strike correlation) and across every duration bucket from intraday to multi-day, so it is not an artifact of hourly churn. C3 CROWDING FALSIFIED IN SIGN: I predicted one-sided books would be WORSE calibrated; they are BETTER (mean |error| 0.199 vs 0.275 balanced, Brier 0.076 vs 0.105). Concentrated flow tracks obvious outcomes rather than crowd error. NOT PROMOTED and NOT TRADABLE ON THIS EVIDENCE: the dataset carries no orderbook, so the pre-registered limitation stands unresolved -- a 21-point gap measured on traded VWAP is not an edge until top-of-book shows the spread does not eat it.
exhibits.about: Kalshi calibration, favourite-longshot bias, and crowding

exhibits.claim: Concentration regime (top-10 share of dollar volume, rolling) conditions the EW-vs-CW spread and cross-sectional signal ICs — rising concentration predicts EW underperformance and IC compression (DESCO Concentration Game 2026)
exhibits.reason: Answered under the concentration_lab study: EW lags CW -3.3%/yr when the market is top-heavy vs -0.75% when broad, but the regime-timed EW/CW tilt fails (t=-0.68). Duplicate; see the concentration tombstone.
exhibits.about: Tests whether trading crowding into a few giant stocks foretells weaker stock-picking signals and lagging small stocks.

exhibits.claim: Gold conditional diversification: stock-bond correlation regime (rolling SPY/TLT) conditions gold allocation value — 60/40 vs 60/35/5+GLD by SB-corr sign (DESCO Worth Its Weight)
exhibits.reason: Answered under the gold_lab study: gold is a real conditional diversifier (19.3%/yr in positive stock-bond-correlation regimes vs 9.8%) but the regime-timed overlay fails the gates (t=-1.04). Duplicate; see the gold tombstone.
exhibits.about: Tests whether gold's value in a stock-bond portfolio depends on whether stocks and bonds move together or apart.

exhibits.claim: Sector-exclusion tilts are factor bets in disguise: ex-energy active returns largely explained by HML loading (DESCO Factored In)
exhibits.reason: Eleven sector exclusions tested on 21 years. Excluding a sector moves the active return by under 1%/yr in every case and only two are even nominally significant (ex-tech -0.73%/yr t=-2.56, ex-consumer-discretionary -0.38%/yr t=-2.41), both NEGATIVE, meaning the exclusion cost money. After FF5+Mom, residual alpha is significant for: ['XLK', 'XLY']. Factor R-squared reaches 0.60 for staples and 0.59 for financials, so the tilt is largely factor exposure by construction. Confirms the DESCO lens: an exclusion is a factor bet until decomposed, and it is not a free ethical or thematic lunch. Tested and shelved.
exhibits.about: Tests whether dropping energy stocks from a portfolio secretly amounts to a bet on cheap versus expensive stocks.

exhibits.claim: AI-adoption language in 10-K filings carries residual alpha after size and factor control (MIT scoring, Increase Alpha's mega-cap critique applied from the start)
exhibits.reason: 14,155 EDGAR filings across 406 names scored for AI vocabulary per 10,000 words. AI language exploded 76x (0.01 in 2015 to 0.76 in 2026), but it does NOT predict returns: Fama-MacBeth t=1.80 controlling for momentum, reversal and size, and as a traded long-high/short-low book it LOST money (Sharpe -0.61, NW t=-2.12, stressed -1.20), failing every gate. DECLARED LIMITATION: term counting cannot distinguish 'we are deploying AI' from 'AI threatens our business' in risk factors, so the score mixes adoption with disclosed threat. A sentiment-aware or section-aware score is the honest follow-up. Talking about AI is not AI alpha.
exhibits.about: MIT scored S&P 500 AI adoption from SEC filings; a replicator found the return premium vanishes once the 38 biggest companies leave the sample - the AI premium may be mega-cap beta in costume. I test adoption with the confounder control built in from day one.

exhibits.claim: Fama-MacBeth cross-sectional panel: which characteristics are priced in US large caps once momentum, reversal, volatility, size, illiquidity and short-volume positioning are held constant
exhibits.reason: Fama-MacBeth on 5,170 dates (348 names/date). Controlling for each other, momentum is NOT priced (t=1.22) and illiquidity is not either over the full history (t=1.26). Short-term reversal is the strongest price characteristic (t=3.29, +3.9%/yr GROSS), with a size effect (t=-2.86) and a volatility premium (t=2.78). This independently reproduces the Alpha158 verdict by a different method: the cross-section is short-term reversal in disguise, and reversal is precisely what the cost-stress book destroys. In the FINRA window the short-volume ratio carries the right sign (heavily shorted underperform) but is insignificant (t=-1.42, and -0.52 against price controls). Gross, before costs; no promotion.
exhibits.about: cross-sectional panel regression, all characteristics at once

exhibits.claim: Disclosure text-change predicts returns (Cohen-Malloy-Nguyen 'Lazy Prices'): when a firm rewrites its 10-Q/10-K vs the prior year, its stock underperforms
exhibits.reason: 14,155 EDGAR 10-Q/10-K filings, 406 names. A year-over-year cosine text-change measure is methodology-sensitive and does NOT replicate Lazy Prices here: cleaned and seasonally controlled it is significant but OPPOSITE-signed (biggest changers slightly outperformed, low-minus-high -1.97%/qtr, |t|=2.55) and well below the stressed promotion bar (~raw t>=5). Most likely a survivorship artifact -- the informative short leg (changers heading for trouble) is delisted out of a current-constituents panel. A clean test needs survivorship-free data (CRSP). Tested and shelved; the vault holds at two.
exhibits.about: EDGAR filing-language change (forensic text, orthogonal)

exhibits.claim: Regime-timed equal-weight/cap-weight tilt: lean to equal-weight when market concentration is falling, cap-weight when rising
exhibits.reason: Concentration is a real descriptive regime — EW lags CW -3.3%/yr when top-heavy vs -0.75%/yr when broad — but the regime-timed EW/CW tilt earns -1.28%/yr at NW t=-0.68 (bar 2.5), fails. A real regime, not a tradable signal; mirrors the gold result. Tested, shelved.
exhibits.about: market concentration / breadth regime (topical macro)

exhibits.claim: Regime-timed gold overlay: hold gold when the stock-bond correlation is positive (bonds stop hedging), a tradable macro-diversification signal
exhibits.reason: Gold returned more in the positive stock-bond-correlation regime (19.3%/yr vs 9.8%), but its 60/40 vol-reduction is regime-invariant (~0.4-0.6%, slightly better when bonds hedge), and the regime-timed overlay earns -3.86%/yr at NW t=-1.04 (bar 2.5) -- fails. Gold is a real diversifier, not a tradable regime signal. Tested and shelved.
exhibits.about: gold as a conditional diversifier (macro/regime)

exhibits.claim: Short-side crowding (FINRA daily short-volume ratio) predicts large-cap cross-sectional returns, and flags stress underperformance
exhibits.reason: Free FINRA short-volume panel (2006 days x 406 names, 2017-12-29..2026-07-24). Family of 4 cross-sectional SVR signals all fail the deflated bar t>=2.96 (best |t|=2.24). Conditional risk measure is loud — most-shorted minus least-shorted = +220.4 bps/mo over 9 worst months (NW t=5.34) — but survivorship-biased (surviving squeezes, not collapses) and small-sample. A risk measure, not a signal; mirrors the 13F crowding study. Tested and shelved.
exhibits.about: FINRA short-volume positioning (free, orthogonal)

exhibits.claim: End-of-quarter window-dressing effect (Altucher #12): returns around quarter turns, equal-weight universe
exhibits.reason: Quarter-end spread +5.87 bps/day, gross +0.89%/yr, NW t=0.83 — not significant against the deflated 3.03 bar. Tested and shelved.
exhibits.about: Altucher calendar/flow family (non-price market-timing)

exhibits.claim: Option-expiration-week effect (Altucher #14): the five days ending on the 3rd-Friday expiry, a dealer-positioning calendar
exhibits.reason: Expiry week underperforms mildly (4.62 bps/day, gross 2.09%/yr) at only NW t=-1.19; no gate-clearing edge either direction. Tested and shelved.
exhibits.about: Altucher calendar/flow family (non-price market-timing)

exhibits.claim: Weekend / Monday effect (Altucher day-of-week family): Mondays vs the rest of the week, equal-weight universe
exhibits.reason: Weekend effect has decayed: Mondays underperform by ~6.62 bps/day but only at NW t=-1.35 gross, it reverses post-2013 (subperiod t 0.99->1.19->1.29->-0.22), and twice-weekly rebalancing costs (~4.71%/yr) swamp the ~2.54%/yr gross. A loud -3.86 in the raw run was a cost-drift artifact. Tested and shelved.
exhibits.about: Altucher calendar/flow family (non-price market-timing)

exhibits.claim: Pre-holiday effect (Altucher / Ariel 1990): last trading day before a market holiday, equal-weight universe
exhibits.reason: Pre-holiday days average +14.82 bps vs the rest, a real magnitude — but only ~3% of days: gross +1.33%/yr at NW t=2.11, below even the naive 2.5 bar and well under the family-deflated 3.03. Underpowered, tested and shelved.
exhibits.about: Altucher calendar/flow family (non-price market-timing)

exhibits.claim: The Alpha158 excavation: Microsoft Qlib's 158 public technical alphas, run as ONE family through the museum's gates - how many famous library alphas survive honest deflation?
exhibits.reason: Alpha158 family (158 alphas): 29 clear naive t>=2.5, 0 are promoted. The strongest member, IMAX20, DOES clear the deflated bar (t=4.46 >= 4.11) and the margin-of-safety rerun (stressed t=3.68 >= 2.50); it is stopped by 55% in-sample to out-of-sample Sharpe degradation (1.14 -> 0.52) against a 30% limit. The null is produced by decay, not by multiplicity. The zoo is short-term reversal + vol risk-premium in disguise. Tested and shelved as one family. [Corrected 2026-08-04: the original reason read '0 survive the deflated bar t>=4.1', which conflated the deflated significance gate with the overall verdict and contradicted Working Paper No. 13. Original text retained in this note.]
exhibits.about: A public library of 158 alphas that half the industry has mined is the perfect multiplicity teaching exhibit: with the family honestly declared at n=158, the deflator does to a famous alpha library what it did to my own founder's model. Museum series material.

exhibits.claim: Tax-loss-selling bounce (Manual of Ideas Table 8.1, 'end-of-year tax selling'): stocks most depressed into year-end (biggest YTD losers) outperform in January as tax-loss selling pressure lifts
exhibits.reason: January tax-loss bounce: worst-decile losers beat the panel by +179bps over Dec20-Jan31, NW t=2.20 on 20 years - the classic January effect does not clear the museum bar in the recent large-cap era (survivorship-biased panel, ~20 obs); Table 8.1 row 1, tested and shelved
exhibits.about: Distinct from my rejected TLH-cost study: this is the OPPORTUNITY side - buying the victims of December tax-loss selling for the January bounce. Table 8.1's first row, made testable.

exhibits.claim: HML redundancy on home turf: is the value factor subsumed by RMW+CMA+Mom in my US large-cap panel 2005-2026, as Fama-French (2015) claimed for the US - or does it retain alpha, as post-2015 international evidence finds?
exhibits.reason: no promotable factor alpha: HML redundant in US large-cap (alpha -0.4%/yr full, +0.9%/yr post-2015, |t|<0.3 both) - a clean replication of Fama-French 2015's US redundancy result; CMA also redundant (t=0.25); only RMW carries marginal standalone alpha (3.4%/yr, t=2.4) below the deflated bar. The value factor being redundant AT HOME while the global literature finds it non-redundant ABROAD is the segmentation thesis in one regression.
exhibits.about: Fama-French declared HML redundant in the US in 2015 (subsumed by profitability and investment). A 2026 deep-research sweep found HML is NOT redundant internationally. Simplest honest question: is it redundant in OUR specific US large-cap, survivorship-biased, recent-era panel? A clean replication with a public verdict either way.
Buys companies whose number of shares outstanding has grown above its own six-month average.
Buys companies whose most conservative analyst estimate of cash flow per share has risen above its own six-month average.
Within each industry, buys companies whose options-market expectation of future price swings has risen the most over the past six months relative to their peers.

exhibits.reason: LOW_SHARPE, LOW_FITNESS, LOW_TURNOVER, CONCENTRATED_WEIGHT, LOW_SUB_UNIVERSE_SHARPE, SELF_CORRELATION

Buys companies whose analyst-estimated pre-tax profit measure stands unusually high relative to their analyst-estimated financing cash flow.
Buys companies whose total after-tax income, including gains and losses outside ordinary earnings, has risen the most over the past two weeks.

exhibits.claim: Statistical jump model as stage-5 challenger (Shu-Yu-Mulvey 2024): temporal k-means with an explicit jump penalty identifies more persistent regimes than my HMM - a regime-aware SPY/cash rule on SJM signals beats the SAME rule on HMM signals out-of-sample
exhibits.reason: challenger fails to displace the incumbent: SJM-rule vs HMM-rule monthly diff +17.5bps/mo, NW t=0.68 (statistical noise; gates need 2.5 and stressed 2.5). On the 2017-2026 SPY testbed the incumbent HMM delivered the BETTER risk profile (Sharpe 0.86 vs 0.70, maxDD -11% vs -25%) at the cost of more switching (36 vs 6); SJM's persistence (avg regime 343 days, 94% risk-on) made it nearly buy-and-hold. Both timing rules trail buy-and-hold on raw return (t~-1.2 each) - regime timing is drawdown insurance here, not growth, consistent with my trend-sleeve verdict. DECLARED LIMITS: simplified protocol, single asset, one allocation rule. Stage-5 HMM keeps its seat - earned in public, not by inertia.
exhibits.about: My regime auditor is an HMM. A Princeton ORFE paper claims the statistical jump model - k-means through time with a penalty for switching - is more robust and persistent. Incumbent vs challenger, same allocation rule, same data, out-of-sample. If the challenger wins, the museum's own stage 5 goes under review; if it loses, the HMM earns its seat in public.

exhibits.claim: The index effect is dead, officially: S&P 500 additions no longer earn announcement-to-inclusion abnormal returns (Greenwood-Sammon), yet index-rebalancing desks reportedly print — test where the residual edge migrated
exhibits.reason: index effect confirmed dead in the panel era: post-effective CARs are statistical zero in all three eras (2005-14: -97bps t=-0.8; 2015-19: +1bp t=0.0; 2020+: -35bps t=-0.2); the only above-Bonferroni window (+170bps pre-effective 2020+, t=2.43) is announcement-runup contamination by construction and still fails the museum bar; deletions untestable (n=11 of 383 in panel - survivorship cap declared). Consistent with Greenwood-Sammon's disappearing index effect.
exhibits.about: The oldest 'free lunch' in indexing - buy the stock entering the S&P before the trackers must - reportedly shrank to nothing (Greenwood-Sammon). Yet the largest platforms' index-rebal teams are cited as top earners. Either the effect is dead and the desks earn something subtler, or the death is exaggerated. A verdict either way is museum-grade.

exhibits.claim: Crowded-exit risk: stocks with high hedge-fund ownership overlap (13F-derived, point-in-time by filing date) underperform specifically during vol-spike windows — the pod-liquidation cascade priced as a conditional factor (Young&Calculated pod-contagion mechanism; Patterson/DESCO lenses as priors)
exhibits.reason: comovement diff +0.009 (t=4.09), stress spread -142bps (t=-3.90, n=14) — neither claim clears the deflated stressed bar
exhibits.about: Bets that stocks owned by the same many hedge funds get hit hardest when those funds all rush the exit at once.

exhibits.claim: Asness equal-risk benchmark: inverse-volatility weighting of the 7Twelve 12-ETF sleeve beats its equal-weight version and 60/40 SPY/AGG
exhibits.reason: inverse-vol 7Twelve: -4.00%/yr vs equal-weight (t=-1.63), -6.59%/yr vs 60/40 (t=-3.58) — risk-weighting was not the missing ingredient either
exhibits.about: Cliff Asness's argument (via Busca podcast): weighting by inverse volatility is the benchmark no optimizer reliably beats. Equal-weight 7Twelve just died; this asks whether risk-weighting, not asset count, was the missing ingredient.
Bets against companies whose news and social-media sentiment has climbed far above its own six-month average.
Buys stocks where the options market's gauge of downside fear has risen the most over the past three months.
Buys companies whose acquired intangible assets have grown most above their own six-month average.

exhibits.claim: Consumer-credit deterioration predicts consumer-finance equity underperformance: rising card delinquency rates (FRED DRCCLACBS, release-date aligned) lead relative returns of consumer lenders vs market (KKR JD stress-scenario translation)
exhibits.reason: rising-vs-falling delinquency: -1.2pct/qtr relative, t=-0.51 on 87 quarters — declared-underpowered test, honest inconclusive
exhibits.about: Watches Americans falling behind on credit cards and bets the lenders' stocks feel it after the data drops.

exhibits.claim: 7Twelve multi-asset equal-weight (Israelsen 2010) beats 60/40 and SPY on geometric growth and drawdown via cross-asset-class breadth

Two honest caveats: (1) survivorship interaction — on a basket of today's S&P survivors every deep loser recovers by construction, so a rule that exits drawdowns is structurally punished; the measured bleed is an upper bound. (2) single-name correlation replacement is crude vs a tracking-error optimizer — the implementation IS the product (the Parametric moat). Mechanism not retestable without point-in-time constituents + contribution flows.

exhibits.claim: Heston neural forward-approximator: params->IV surface to <0.5 vol pt with >=100x speedup (Horvath-Muguruza-Tomas program)
exhibits.reason: CORRECTED 2026-07-29 (audit of vault against published notes, per lessons/rerun-verdicts-must-overwrite.md rule 2). The original reason recorded here, 'MAE 66.86 vp / speedup 51684x missed gates', was a BUG ARTIFACT, not a finding: a one-line bisection error pinned every implied vol at 150%, and a degenerate-case test (vol-of-vol -> 0 must recover Black-Scholes) caught it. The rev2 run PASSED every pre-set gate: 0.23 vol-point MAE (worst 11.8) on 9,000 self-generated surfaces, ~45,182x speedup vs characteristic-function integration, skew sanity pass; published in Working Paper No. 2 'Neural Pricing'. THIS ROW REMAINS status='rejected' DELIBERATELY, and not because the technique failed. The Heston surrogate is a PRICING TOOL that passed its own approximation gates, not an alpha edge that cleared stage 4/6, so counting it as a vault survivor would conflate two different claims and inflate the public survivor count. Promotion, if ever wanted, is the owner's gate. READ THIS BEFORE APPLYING CLAUDE.md RULE 2: do NOT treat neural approximation of a known pricing map as a dead idea. It works. What died was neural FORECASTING of financial series (chain v1.5 MLP, NW t=-4.37; zero-shot Kronos, DM t=-12.37). See docs/neural_house_view.md: data density, not model capacity, decides.
exhibits.about: Trains a neural network to imitate a slow options-pricing model, trading a long calculation for an instant lookup.
